question.value: Investigate the physical and chemical properties, molecular abundances, and origin of cold CH$_3$OH gas in two dense molecular cloud cores (N79S-1 and N79S-2) offset from the SSC candidate H72.97-69.39 in the low-metallicity N79 region of the LMC.

evidence.quote: In this study, we report the detection of cold ($\leq$ 15 K) CH$_3$OH gas towards two dense cores, which are located $\sim$ 1.2 pc offset from the super star cluster (SSC) candidate (H72.97-69.39) in the N79 region of the LMC.
The possible origins of cold CH$_3$OH gas in these dense cores are discussed, along with a possible explanation for the non-detection of CH$_3$OH in the SSC candidate.
Observations were carried out with ALMA as part of the Cycle 5 (2017.1.01323.S) and Cycle 6 (2018.1.01366.S) programs (PI: T. Shimonishi).
Observations were carried out with ALMA as part of the Cycle 5 (2017.1.01323.S) and Cycle 6 (2018.1.01366.S) programs (PI: T. Shimonishi).
To investigate whether the observed molecules are related to shock chemistry, we compare their spatial distribution with CO outflows observed in ALMA Cycle 7 (ID: 2019.1.01770.S).

claims.hypothesis: Cold CH3OH can be efficiently formed in low-metallicity LMC molecular clouds if local regions are sufficiently cold, dense, and well-shielded from the strong interstellar UV field.
claims.experiment: Performed 0.4'' (0.1 pc) resolution ALMA Band 6 and 7 continuum and spectral line observations of N79S-1 and N79S-2, deriving gas temperatures via CH3OH and SO rotation diagrams and abundances relative to dust-derived N(H2).
claims.finding: Despite the lower metallicity in the LMC, CH3OH abundance in N79S-1 is comparable to Galactic cold cores without metallicity correction, confirming efficient CH3OH production in cold, dense, well-shielded cores.

evidence.quote: The rotation diagram analysis of CH$_3$OH and SO lines yields an average gas temperature of 13 $\pm$ 0.4 K for N79S-1 and 15 $\pm$ 0.9 K for N79S-2.
Despite the lower metallicity in the LMC, the CH$_3$OH abundance at N79S-1 is comparable to that of similar cold sources in our Galaxy.
The present observational results suggest that the CH$_3$OH can be produced adequately in a low metallicity environment if the region is cold, dense, and well-shielded.

claims.hypothesis: The non-detection of CH3OH toward the luminous SSC candidate H72.97-69.39 is caused by strong UV/X-ray radiation and high-temperature gas-phase destruction at a more evolved YSO stage.

claims.finding: Strong UV/X-ray radiation and high temperatures from newly born stars in the SSC candidate likely destroy CH3OH or alter its chemical evolution.

evidence.quote: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) is an excellent target for studying the formation and survival of COMs in low metallicity regions.

limitations_admitted.value: Some CH3OH transitions (especially 1_1-0_0 A+) and the H2CO transition are moderately to highly optically thick according to RADEX, making the H2CO column density a lower limit.

evidence.quote: Among these, three have optical depths of approximately 1, while the 1$_1$-0$_0$ A$^+$ line has a significantly higher optical depth of 5.3.
Therefore, the H$_2$CO line is moderately optically thick in both sources. In this study, the derived column density of H$_2$CO may be considered a lower limit for both sources.

limitations_admitted.value: Derived molecular abundances can be affected by spatial filtering, excitation temperature assumptions, optical depth, and beam filling factors, while only dust temperature uncertainty (10-20 K) is folded into N(H2).

evidence.quote: The derived abundances of the observed molecules may be significantly affected by several factors, including spatial filtering effects, assumptions about excitation temperature, optical depth, and beam filling factors. In this work, we consider only the temperature uncertainty when estimating H$_2$ column densities from dust continuum observations.

referee_caveats_inferred: Three CH3OH lines (5_-1-4_-1 E, 5_0-4_0 A+, 4_0-3_-1 E) in N79S-1 have optical depths ~1 in RADEX but were retained in the optically thin LTE rotation diagram fit.
Only two SO transitions in N79S-1 and three in N79S-2 were used to fit a straight line in the SO rotation diagram.

Using the arithmetic mean of 10 K and 20 K column densities as the nominal value biases the central estimate toward the 10 K value because the Planck function and partition functions are non-linear in temperature.
